content: The Seventeen Rules of Enjuin were a code of conduct established for students of the Japanese Ri-shu school of medicine in the 16th century CE. These rules were akin to the Hippocratic Oath, emphasizing the ethical responsibilities of physicians. 1. Every individual must follow the path ordained by Heaven, which refers to Buddha or the gods. 2. Always treat others with kindness and maintain a deep devotion to loving humanity. 3. The teaching of medicine should be limited to carefully selected individuals. 4. Do not disclose the medical knowledge or treatments you have been taught without explicit permission. 5. Avoid forming associations with physicians who are not affiliated with this school. 6. All successors and descendants of the disciples of this school must adhere to the teachings and practices of their instructors. 7. If a disciple ceases to practice medicine or if no successors are found upon their death, all medical texts belonging to this school must be returned to the School of Enjuin. 8. Do not kill living beings, and refrain from admiring or engaging in hunting or fishing. 9. Teaching about poisons is strictly forbidden within this school, and you must not receive instructions about poisons from other physicians. Additionally, you must not provide abortive substances to anyone. 10. You must provide care even to patients you dislike or hate. Perform virtuous acts discreetly, as true virtue lies in doing good without seeking recognition. 11. Avoid greed and do not strive for fame. Never rebuke or reproach a patient, even if they fail to offer you money or goods in gratitude. 12. If a patient you have treated unsuccessfully is cured by another physician, you should feel joy rather than resentment. 13. Refrain from speaking ill of other physicians. 14. When entering a woman’s room for medical purposes, do not disclose what you observe or learn, and ensure that your thoughts and actions remain free of any obscene or immoral intent. 15. Do not share the knowledge you gain from lectures or the details of medical prescriptions with others, whether appropriate or not. 16. Avoid indulgence in undue extravagance. Such a lifestyle fosters greed and diminishes your capacity for kindness toward others. 17. If you fail to abide by the rules and regulations of this school, your status as a disciple will be revoked. In more severe cases, the punishment will be harsher. These rules reflect a strict ethical framework designed to guide the behavior, practice, and moral integrity of physicians within the Enjuin school of medicine.
